findings.issue: Spent ~8 turns debugging a 'wrong selected option' that was stale browser cache from the pre-fix build; after rebuilding, it restarted the server but not the browser session and kept re-probing
findings.suggestion: When tests pass but a manual probe disagrees, distrust the dev environment first (restart browser/clear cache) before re-inspecting SSR and hydration internals

findings.issue: `agent-browser screenshot /tmp/shot-home.png --full-page` — flag parsed as filename, wrote a file named `--full-page` and lost the screenshot
findings.suggestion: Check `agent-browser screenshot --help` for the full-page flag syntax before using it

findings.issue: Three web_fetch failures on docs.solidjs.com v2 pages (URL guessing) before falling back to curl and the GitHub templates
findings.suggestion: Fall back to curl or the search result URLs sooner; the successful fetch in turn 24 already pointed at the right URL pattern

findings.issue: `pkill -f "node .output/server/index.mjs"` matched its own wrapping bash process, killing the shell (exit 143)
findings.suggestion: Use a more specific pattern or `pkill -f` excluding the current shell, or record the PID at server start

findings.issue: 48k-character thinking block before scaffolding; large reasoning bursts inflate cost/latency without adding tool efficiency
findings.suggestion: Split design into per-file decisions made at write time

summary: A near-exemplary autonomous session: it read the spec, tests and every reference screenshot up front, verified the current SolidStart 2.x API against docs and official templates before writing code, and produced a working app in one forward pass with 51/54 tests passing on first run and a single surgical fix cycle. Verification was thorough (full suite after each change, 7 screenshots compared to references at both widths, a final clean-pipeline run) and it even improved fidelity beyond test requirements. The only real blemish is ~8 turns spent chasing a stale-cache artifact in its own dev browser session, plus minor tool-call fumbles.
